newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The presidential palace belittles the unification of three opposition parties, predicting the merger will break up in two months due to conflicting ambitions (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Eighty seven senior congressmen who want to lift their term limits may oust House speaker Jose de Venecia from his post since he is against extending term limits. (TODAY)
- Vice president Joseph Estrada urges President Fidel Ramos to concentrate on economic bills instead of attempting to amend the Constitution (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- President Fidel Ramos warns against the prevalence of partisan politics, saying this can divide the country and set back the gains it has achieved.
- MBf Holdings Bhd is set to acquire 60 percent of Prime Savings Bank for an initial investment of 500 million pesos. (ALL PAPERS)
- The Department of Agriculture has promised to modify its new policy reducing import tariffs on a range of agricultural products (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Central Bank is realigning the consortium of lead managers for its $1.25 billion long-term global bond offering this year. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Victorias Milling Co and its creditor banks are set to meet today to thresh out the issue of unsecured refined sugar delivery orders/receipts. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
